name: Wasp
summary: The founding Avenger who named the team. Janet van Dyne shrinks to insect size, flies on wings and stings with bio-electric blasts, and she has chaired the Avengers more than once.
origin: The Wasp is the founding Avenger who named the team, and she deserves more credit for it. Janet van Dyne arrived in Tales to Astonish #44 in 1963, from Stan Lee, Ernie Hart and Jack Kirby, as a wealthy young woman who teamed up with scientist Hank Pym after her father was killed by an alien. Pym gave her the ability to shrink and sprout wings, and she later learned to fire stinging bio-electric blasts and command insects. Months later she was there with Thor, the Hulk, Ant-Man and Iron Man when the Avengers formed, and she has led the team more than once. She is also a fashion designer who changes costumes constantly.
powers: Shrinks to insect size and back

storyline.title: A partner for Pym
storyline.beat: Janet van Dyne asks scientist Hank Pym for help avenging her father's murder. He gives her the power to shrink and grow wings, and she becomes the Wasp.

storyline.title: Naming the team
storyline.beat: Janet is a founding member of the Avengers and suggests the team's name in its first issue.

storyline.title: Wedding to Hank
storyline.beat: Janet marries Hank Pym, then going by Yellowjacket, in Avengers #60.

storyline.title: Chairwoman
storyline.beat: After her divorce Janet becomes one of the Avengers' longest-serving leaders.

storyline.title: Lost and found
storyline.beat: Janet seems to die at the end of Secret Invasion, but she is later found alive in the Microverse.

storyline.title: Nadia van Dyne
storyline.beat: Hank's daughter Nadia, raised in Russia, takes up the Wasp name. Janet becomes her mentor.

gossip.text: She named the Avengers in their very first issue.
Hope van Dyne was the original Wasp in the comics.
gossip.truth: Janet van Dyne was the original Wasp in 1963. Hope comes from the films.

gossip.text: She is a fashion designer and has changed costumes more often than almost any other Avenger.
Avengers #213 (1981), where Hank strikes Janet, became one of Marvel's most notorious moments. Editor Jim Shooter later said the art was meant to look like an accident.
Hank's daughter Nadia took the Wasp name in 2016.

quiz.q: Which founding member gave the Avengers their name?
quiz.why: Janet suggested the name in Avengers #1.

quiz.q: What is Janet van Dyne's career?
Who was the Wasp's original partner?
quiz.why: Hank Pym gave her powers in 1963.

theme.tagline: Tiny, winged and absolutely running this meeting.

timeline.title: A partner for Pym
timeline.note: Tales to Astonish #44 introduces Janet van Dyne, who gains wings and shrinking powers.

timeline.title: Naming the team
timeline.note: The Avengers #1 has Janet suggest the team's name, a fact fans love to repeat.

timeline.title: Wedding to Hank Pym
timeline.note: Avengers #60 holds Janet's wedding to Hank, who shows up as the new Yellowjacket.

timeline.title: Chairwoman of the Avengers
timeline.note: Avengers #217 has Janet leading the team, one of its longest-serving chairs.

timeline.title: Earth's Mightiest Heroes
timeline.note: The Avengers: Earth's Mightiest Heroes cartoon makes Janet a founding team member on TV.

timeline.title: Back from the Microverse
timeline.note: After being presumed dead in Secret Invasion, Avengers #32 finds Janet alive and rescues her.

timeline.title: Nadia van Dyne arrives
timeline.note: Hank's long-lost daughter Nadia debuts and later becomes the Unstoppable Wasp.

timeline.title: Michelle Pfeiffer's Janet
timeline.note: Ant-Man and the Wasp pulls Michelle Pfeiffer's Janet out of the Quantum Realm.
